note: Re-judged 2026-10-20 (independent judge 15, after e8e3ea3f6e). Section 2.21.4: "A node receiving a suspicious message from an IP address (and port, if NAT traversal is used) with which it has an IKE SA SHOULD send an IKE Notify payload in an IKE INFORMATIONAL exchange over that SA." The only judged-unit change is the new positive TestSusOwnerLoopPublishesMovedEndpoint, which closes judge 14's finding that no test ran maintainSA's publish. It runs the real maintainSA with the configured remote moved to 127.0.0.9 and sa.peerEndpoint at the peer's address, waits for the loop to publish (fatal if it never does) and asserts the published IP/port equal the SA's endpoint, hands an out-of-SA INFORMATIONAL request from that endpoint to noteSuspicious, and asserts one datagram that is INFORMATIONAL, not marked response, carries the SA's two SPIs, decrypts and authenticates under the peer's copy of the SA keys, holds exactly one payload, a Notify of type INVALID_IKE_SPI; after closing stopCh and joining the loop, a drain proves no second datagram, saEndpoint is nil, and the same packet is not queued to ps.suspicious. Claim matches the body; 'queued to no session' is asserted on the one registered session's queue, which is the only session in activePeersMap here. The post-exit check discriminates the new defer ps.saEndpoint.Store(nil): the test calls maintainSA directly, so ownedSA (cleared by runEstablished, not maintainSA) stays set from susRegister and only the withdrawn endpoint stops the match. Mutant record present and verified by ./le rfc check (no violation listed): established.go::maintainSA line 274 'ps.publishSAEndpoint(sa)' -> '_ = sa', producer sha f52db92f225348aa, consistent with the deleted call making susAwaitPublished fail. The four earlier Sus units are unchanged; negative polarity carriers unchanged. All five TestSus tests PASS at HEAD under -race. Judge 14's remaining minor notes (first map-order match only; remoteUDPAddr udp4 for IPv6 configured remote, journaled as IPv4-only IKE transport) stand with no verdict effect.
